      How to Use the Random Number Generator

      Set the lowest and highest number you want, then how many numbers to make, from 1 to 100. Negative numbers work. Tap Generate. Switch to Decimals for numbers like 3.14, with up to 6 decimal places. Turn off Allow repeats when every number has to be different, like drawing raffle tickets.

      How the numbers are picked

      Every number in your range has the same chance. The numbers come from your browser's secure random number generator (the same one used for encryption), not the predictable kind built into most simple scripts. With repeats off, each number is drawn from what's left, like pulling tickets out of a hat.

      It all happens on your device. Your range and results aren't sent anywhere or saved, and they're gone when you close the tab.

      Ways to use it

      • Raffles. Number the tickets, then draw winners with repeats off.
      • Picking a page or question. Set the range to the page count or the number of questions.
      • Classroom draws. Give each student a number and generate one.
      • Who goes first. Everyone guesses a number from 1 to 100; closest wins.
      • Lottery-style practice numbers. Fine for fun, but random picks don't change your odds of winning a real lottery. Nothing does.

      Frequently Asked Questions

      Is it really random?

      Yes. Every number in the range has the same chance, and the numbers come from your browser's secure random number generator, which is built for encryption and isn't predictable.

      Can I generate numbers without repeats?

      Turn off Allow repeats. Each number can then come up only once, so you can ask for up to as many numbers as the range holds. 1 to 10, for example, gives at most 10.

      What range can I use?

      Any whole numbers from −1,000,000,000 to 1,000,000,000, as long as the maximum is bigger than the minimum. Both ends are included, so 1 to 100 can give 1 or 100.

      Can I generate decimals?

      Yes. Choose Decimals and pick 0 to 6 decimal places. With 2 places, 1 to 2 can give anything from 1.00 to 2.00.

      Is my input uploaded anywhere?

      No. The numbers are made in your browser. Nothing you type is sent to a server or saved.
